chunks: There is no harm for the blind, nor for the lame, nor for the sick,

nor for yourselves, that you eat from your own houses, or the houses of your fathers, or your mothers, or your brothers, or your sisters, or your paternal uncles, or your paternal aunts, or your maternal uncles, or your maternal aunts, or from the houses whose keys you possess, or from the houses of your friends.
There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately.
When you enter houses, give salutations to yourselves, a greeting from Allah, blessed and good.
Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses, that you may use your intellect.
ai.seo_question: What are the permissible places to eat according to Surah An-Nur and what is the etiquette of entering a house?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited alongside the preceding verses on modesty, clarifies that the prohibition of entering homes without permission applies specifically to non-mahram interactions, thereby exempting close kin and friends from strict formalities. Shia scholars highlight the detailed enumeration of relatives to emphasize the warmth and accessibility of family bonds, while the command to greet oneself ('salimoo anfusikum') is interpreted by some exegetes as a reminder of self-accountability or a general greeting to all present. It serves as a practical legal framework for social gatherings, balancing privacy with communal ease.
